connections.environment: Color and protection: a new prod connection is read-only, and every change on it asks you to type the connection name.
connections.readOnly: Glafira will not change anything in the cluster through this connection, whatever your rights are.
connections.apiUrl: The API server, as in oc login or kubeconfig: usually https://api.cluster:6443; a path is allowed (Rancher proxy). Not the web console.
connections.authMethod: Browser — OpenShift OAuth, like oc login --web. Token — oc whoami -t or a service account token. Certificate — PEM. Exec plugin — a command from kubeconfig.
connections.token: Saved in the system secret store, not in a file. Tokens from OpenShift OAuth usually expire after 24 hours.
connections.clientCert: Certificate and key in PEM format. The key is saved in the system secret store.
connections.exec: Only allowed commands: aws, aws-iam-authenticator, gke-gcloud-auth-plugin, kubelogin, kubectl oidc-login, oc, yc, rancher. Run without a shell; may open the browser.
connections.execLine: Exactly what Glafira will run. Values of variables and options that look like secrets are hidden. Any change to the line needs a new confirmation.
connections.ca: System store — the CAs trusted by your computer. Certificates — only the listed ones, like certificate-authority in kubeconfig.
connections.tlsServerName: Only if the certificate is issued for another name than the address host. Usually empty.
connections.proxy: System — the HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY variables. Or an explicit address like http://proxy:3128.
connections.favorites: Shown first in the tree. Separate with commas.
connections.manualNamespaces: If the cluster does not let you list projects, list the ones you work with here.
connections.test: Checks step by step: address, TLS, sign-in, platform and projects. Unsaved fields are tested too.
connections.llmAccess: What an LLM assistant over MCP may read. Metadata: objects, statuses, events — no env, ConfigMap or Secret values. With logs: also pod logs, env and ConfigMap values, masked. Off: nothing.
connections.llmScope: Projects the LLM may read; an empty list means it sees no projects. The cluster itself and nodes stay visible if you can read them. The setting stays on this computer: export does not write it.
connections.metrics: Automatic: Thanos Querier on OpenShift, Prometheus through the API server elsewhere, then metrics.k8s.io. Own: a Thanos or Prometheus address. Not exported.
connections.metricsAuth: Connection token — the token of this connection. Own token — saved in the system secret store. A token is sent only over https.
connections.mask: The list replaces the standard one. Not exported: each user decides it.

cluster.platform: Detected from the API groups and the version: OpenShift, or Kubernetes with its distribution (EKS, GKE, AKS, Rancher, Deckhouse, k3s, RKE2).
cluster.apiGroups: What the cluster offers beyond plain Kubernetes: Route, projects and DeploymentConfig (OpenShift), Gateway API. They decide which objects are shown.
cluster.readyz: The /readyz checks of the API server. Any user can read them; a failed check names the part of the server that is not ready.

kubeconfig.target: New connections go to this folder; connections that already exist keep their place, name, environment and color.

import.target: Where new folders and connections go. Existing ones stay where they are.
import.updateExisting: Connections that already exist get the settings from the file; your tokens, keys and their place in the tree are kept.

logs.filter: The filter runs in Glafira before the lines reach the window: a substring or a regular expression (regex). Lines that do not match are counted but not shown.

settings.mcpEnable: Starts a local MCP server for LLM assistants. Access is opened per connection and is off by default; each new client is confirmed in a dialog.
settings.mcpResponseLimit: Largest answer one tool call returns to the LLM. Choose a smaller limit for a local model with a small context (64k tokens or less).
settings.mcpCompact: Hides the tools for notes and change proposals from this client: their descriptions take about 2,300 tokens of a local model's context. The client sees the new list after it reconnects.

health.check: Runs the built-in Glafira rules over the cluster, its nodes and up to 50 projects. Severity depends on the connection environment. The check only reads the cluster.
health.hidden: Findings you hid for a particular object. They are not counted in badges; LLM assistants see them marked as hidden.
health.proposals: A change an LLM assistant suggests. Nothing is applied until you open it in a form and confirm; you can edit the values first.

resources.window: Statistics over the last 1, 7, 14 or 30 days, but not longer than the metrics source keeps. Percentiles are taken per pod, then the worst pod.
resources.confidence: High — window and data of 7 days or more with coverage of 80 % or more; medium — data of 24 hours or more with coverage of 50 % or more; low — less, or only metrics.k8s.io.

mcp.intro: An LLM assistant (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and others) can connect to Glafira over MCP, read the metadata of the connections you open for it, run a cluster check and leave notes; at the “Metadata and logs” level it also reads pod logs and environment and ConfigMap values, with secrets masked. It cannot change anything in the clusters.

about.summary: Glafira is a desktop app for working with Kubernetes clusters and diagnosing them, with OpenShift and Platform V DropApp in focus: connections with a token, a certificate, browser sign-in or an exec plugin, import from kubeconfig, folders and step-by-step connection checks.

cluster.apiNotReady.title: API server is not ready
cluster.apiNotReady.details: /readyz reports failed checks: {{failed}}. Requests to the cluster may fail or be slow until they pass.
cluster.apiNotReady.fix: Check the control plane: etcd, the API server logs and the control-plane nodes.

cluster.operatorDegraded.title: ClusterOperators are degraded or unavailable
cluster.operatorDegraded.fix: Open the operators on the cluster overview: the cause is usually in the pods and events of the operator's project.

cluster.updateFailing.title: Cluster update is failing
cluster.updateFailing.details: ClusterVersion reports Failing=True{{because}}: the cluster cannot complete its update.
cluster.updateFailing.fix: Check the ClusterVersion conditions and the operators that block the update.

cluster.mcpDegraded.title: MachineConfigPools are degraded
cluster.mcpDegraded.details: MachineConfigPools with Degraded=True: {{pools}} (total {{count}}). Nodes of these pools do not get configuration updates.
cluster.mcpDegraded.fix: Check the pool conditions and the machine-config-daemon logs on its nodes.

node.notReady.title: Node {{name}} is not ready
node.notReady.details: The Ready condition is {{status}}{{because}}: pods on the node may be evicted and new pods are not scheduled there.
node.notReady.fix: Check the kubelet and the container runtime on the node, its network and its disk.

node.pressure.title: Node {{name}} is under pressure
node.pressure.details: Conditions that are True: {{conditions}}. The kubelet evicts pods and refuses new ones until the pressure goes away.
node.pressure.fix: Free memory, disk or process IDs on the node, or move some workloads to other nodes.

node.requestsHigh.title: Node {{name}} is almost fully requested
node.requestsHigh.details: Pods on the node request {{cpuPercent}}% of its allocatable CPU and {{memoryPercent}}% of its memory: new pods may not fit.
node.requestsHigh.fix: Add nodes or lower the requests of pods that request more than they use.

node.unschedulable.title: Node {{name}} is cordoned
node.unschedulable.details: spec.unschedulable is set: no new pods are scheduled on the node.
node.unschedulable.fix: If the maintenance is over, uncordon the node (kubectl uncordon).

pod.crashLoop.title: {{object}}: containers restart in a loop
pod.crashLoop.details: Containers {{containers}} keep crashing{{affected}}: last exit {{reason}}, exit code {{exitCode}}, up to {{restarts}} restarts.
pod.crashLoop.fix: Read the logs of the previous run of the container and the pod events: the cause is usually in the application or its configuration.

pod.imagePull.title: {{object}}: image cannot be pulled
pod.imagePull.fix: Check the image name and tag, that the registry is reachable from the nodes, and the pull secret.

pod.pending.title: {{object}}: Pending for too long
pod.pending.details: Pending for more than 5 minutes (up to {{minutes}} min){{affected}}{{because}}.
pod.pending.fix: Look at the pod events: usually the scheduler finds no node with enough resources and matching selectors and tolerations, or a volume is not ready.

pod.oomKilled.title: {{object}}: containers were OOMKilled
pod.oomKilled.details: Containers {{containers}} were killed for exceeding their memory limit in the last 24 hours{{affected}}.
pod.oomKilled.fix: Raise the memory limit or find out why the application needs more memory.

pod.restartsFrequent.title: {{object}}: frequent restarts
pod.restartsFrequent.details: Containers restarted at least 5 times (up to {{restarts}}){{affected}}, the last time {{lastRestartMinutes}} min ago.
pod.restartsFrequent.fix: Read the logs of the previous run and the pod events; check the liveness probe and the memory limit.

workload.unavailable.title: {{object}} is unavailable
workload.unavailable.details: Only {{available}} of {{desired}} desired replicas have been available for more than 5 minutes (about {{minutes}} min).
workload.unavailable.fix: Open the pods and events of the workload and find out why the pods are not ready.

workload.rolloutStuck.title: {{object}}: rollout is stuck
workload.rolloutStuck.details: Progressing=False with ProgressDeadlineExceeded{{because}}: new pods did not become available in time.
workload.rolloutStuck.fix: Check the pods of the new ReplicaSet; roll back if the new version does not start.

workload.singleReplica.title: {{object}} runs a single replica
workload.singleReplica.details: One replica and no HPA: a restart, a node drain or an update makes it unavailable.
workload.singleReplica.detailsHpa: One replica and HPA {{hpa}} with minReplicas = 1: a restart, a node drain or an update makes it unavailable.
workload.singleReplica.fix: Run at least two replicas (or minReplicas ≥ 2) and add a PodDisruptionBudget.

container.noRequests.title: {{object}}: containers without requests
container.noRequests.details: Running containers without a CPU request: {{cpu}}; without a memory request: {{memory}} (after LimitRange defaults).
container.noRequests.detailsCpu: Running containers without a CPU request: {{cpu}} (after LimitRange defaults).
container.noRequests.detailsMemory: Running containers without a memory request: {{memory}} (after LimitRange defaults).
container.noRequests.fix: Set requests close to the real usage: the scheduler places pods by them, and pods without requests are evicted first.

container.noMemoryLimit.title: {{object}}: containers without a memory limit
container.noMemoryLimit.details: Running containers without a memory limit: {{containers}}.
container.noMemoryLimit.fix: Set a memory limit: one leaking container can starve the whole node.

container.noReadinessProbe.title: {{object}}: containers without a readiness probe
container.noReadinessProbe.fix: Add a readiness probe: without it, traffic reaches pods before they are ready, also during rollouts.

container.latestTag.title: {{object}}: images with the latest tag
container.latestTag.details: Running containers use images tagged latest or without a tag: {{images}}.
container.latestTag.fix: Pin a version tag or a digest: otherwise pods may run different versions after restarts.

quota.nearLimit.title: {{object}} is almost used up
quota.nearLimit.fix: Raise the quota or free resources: new pods and objects are rejected once it is exceeded.

pvc.pending.title: {{object}} is {{phase}}
pvc.pending.details: The claim has been Pending for more than 5 minutes (about {{minutes}} min) while pods {{pods}} wait for it (storage class {{class}}).
pvc.pending.detailsLost: The bound volume is lost: pods that use it cannot start.
pvc.pending.fix: Check the storage class, its provisioner and the claim events.

hpa.atMax.title: {{object}} is at its maximum
hpa.atMax.details: ScalingLimited=True with TooManyReplicas: {{target}} needs more than maxReplicas = {{maxReplicas}}.
hpa.atMax.fix: Raise maxReplicas or reduce the load per replica.

hpa.unableToScale.title: {{object}} cannot scale
hpa.unableToScale.details: {{condition}}=False{{because}}: the HPA does not change the replicas of {{target}}.
hpa.unableToScale.fix: Check that metrics are available (metrics-server or an adapter) and that the target pods have requests for the scaled resource.

service.noEndpoints.title: {{object}} has no ready endpoints
service.noEndpoints.details: The Service selects no ready pods: requests to it fail.
service.noEndpoints.detailsUsedBy: The Service selects no ready pods: requests to it fail. It is used by {{referencedBy}}.
service.noEndpoints.fix: Compare the Service selector with the pod labels and find out why the pods are not ready.

route.notAdmitted.title: {{object}} is not admitted
route.notAdmitted.details: Admitted=False{{because}}: the Route does not serve traffic.
route.notAdmitted.detailsNoStatus: No router has admitted the Route (it has no status): it does not serve traffic.
route.notAdmitted.fix: Check whether another Route already uses the host, and the router shard selectors.

route.certExpiring.title: {{object}}: certificate expires
route.certExpiring.details: The certificate in spec.tls expires in {{days}} day(s).
route.certExpiring.detailsExpired: The certificate in spec.tls expired {{daysAgo}} day(s) ago: clients reject the connection.
route.certExpiring.fix: Renew the certificate in the Route.

ingress.classMissing.title: {{object}}: ingress class is missing
ingress.classMissing.details: IngressClass {{class}} does not exist: no controller serves this Ingress.
ingress.classMissing.detailsNoClass: The Ingress names no class and there is no default IngressClass: no controller may serve it.
ingress.classMissing.fix: Set spec.ingressClassName to an existing class or mark one class as the default.

ingress.backendMissing.title: {{object}}: backend is missing
ingress.backendMissing.details: Services that do not exist in the project: {{services}}; ports missing on existing Services: {{ports}}. Requests to these paths fail.
ingress.backendMissing.fix: Fix the backend names and ports in the Ingress rules or create the missing Services.

ingress.tlsSecretMissing.title: {{object}}: TLS Secret is missing
ingress.tlsSecretMissing.details: Secrets from spec.tls have not been found for more than 5 minutes: {{secrets}}. The controller serves its default certificate instead.
ingress.tlsSecretMissing.fix: Create the Secrets or fix their names in spec.tls; check whether cert-manager fails to issue them.

gatewayRoute.notAccepted.title: {{object}} is not accepted
gatewayRoute.notAccepted.details: Gateways {{parents}} did not accept the route{{because}}: its rules do not apply there.
gatewayRoute.notAccepted.fix: Check the parentRefs, the allowedRoutes of the listeners and the hostnames.

gatewayRoute.refsUnresolved.title: {{object}}: references are unresolved
gatewayRoute.refsUnresolved.details: ResolvedRefs=False{{because}} on {{parents}}: some backends are missing or not permitted.
gatewayRoute.refsUnresolved.fix: Check the backendRefs and, for other namespaces, the ReferenceGrant.

gateway.notProgrammed.title: {{object}} is not programmed
gateway.notProgrammed.details: {{condition}}=False for more than 5 minutes{{because}}: the Gateway does not serve traffic.
gateway.notProgrammed.fix: Check the GatewayClass and the controller that implements it.

check.partial.title: The check is incomplete
check.partial.details: Some objects were not checked: {{parts}}. Findings may be missing for them.
check.partial.detailsUnknown: Some objects were not checked: findings may be missing for them.
check.partial.fix: Check as a user who can read more, or check fewer projects; the permissions are on the cluster overview.

resources.cpuThrottled.title: {{object}}: CPU is throttled
resources.cpuThrottled.details: Containers with a CPU limit were throttled on average over the last 24 hours: {{containers}}.
resources.cpuThrottled.fix: Raise the CPU limit or remove it: the limit cuts CPU time and slows responses. The Resources tab shows the usage and a recommendation.

resources.memoryNearLimit.title: {{object}}: memory close to the limit
resources.memoryNearLimit.details: Containers used 90% or more of their memory limit over the last 24 hours (maximum / limit): {{containers}}.
resources.memoryNearLimit.fix: Raise the memory limit or reduce the usage: the next spike may end in OOMKilled. The Resources tab shows the usage and a recommendation.

resources.overProvisioned.title: {{object}}: requests far above the usage
resources.overProvisioned.details: Requests are much higher than the usage over the last 24 hours — CPU (request / p95): {{cpu}}; memory (request / maximum): {{memory}}.
resources.overProvisioned.detailsCpu: Requests are much higher than the usage over the last 24 hours — CPU (request / p95): {{cpu}}.
resources.overProvisioned.detailsMemory: Requests are much higher than the usage over the last 24 hours — memory (request / maximum): {{memory}}.
resources.overProvisioned.fix: Lower the requests closer to the usage: the reserved capacity is unavailable to other pods and counts against the quota. The Resources tab shows a recommendation.
